newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds end lower on interbank.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds end lower on interbank.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended lower across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest following a small hike in the interbank rate, dealers said on Friday.
"Bond prices were marked up down slightly today following a small hike in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly higher but volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.43/98.48 compared with Thursday's close of S$98.50/98.55, September 2001 at S$97.14/97.19 against S$97.25/97.30 and June 2003 at S$95.14/95.19 from S$95.25/95.30.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 2-3/8 2-1/4 percent versus Thursday's 1-7/8 1-3/4 percent.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.92/1.87 percent against Thursday's yield of 1.78/1.73 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.06/2.01 percent from 2.01/1.96 percent.
